title: Unsynchronized Dequeue-Resize Collision
pattern: Performing structural modifications on a collection (e.g. dequeuing from a bucket) while another thread concurrently resizes the collection's backbone array without exclusive lock coordination.
why_bad: It breaks the structural alignment of the collection, leading to pointer corruption, lost elements, or infinite loops in traversal.
detection: A non-thread-safe collection structure where resizing does not acquire the locks of all individual buckets or elements being modified.
counterexample: Using a resizing protocol that locks all buckets (e.g. Java's `ConcurrentHashMap` resizing) or blocks all traversals during a resize.
fix: Coordinate the bucket modifications and resizes with locks or epoch-based synchronization.
